Windwalker Monk Rotation in 

Although Windwalker Monks have one of the most unique Masteries in the game, the spec's playstyle can be simplified into a few important things to remember. The core concepts to keep in mind are these:

 

 

 
 Don't Repeat Abilities: Don't hit the same ability twice in a row. Midnight added a new buff that tracks what button you pressed last, track that buff using the in-game options or another tool.
 

 

 
 

 
 Avoid Overcapping Resources: Windwalker has to manage both Energy and Chi, try to avoid wasting them. There are times where wasting resources cannot be avoided, but as a general rule, try to do this as little as possible.
 

 

 
 

 
 Use Abilities with Cooldowns: Abilities with short cooldowns like and are some of the most important damage abilities you have. Avoid abilities with cooldowns sitting unused as this often leaves to lost damage potential.
 
 

 

 
 

 
 Plan your Usage: has a very flexible cooldown depending on your choice of talents, plan when to use it to maximize its strength. can be a 60, 70, 80, or a 90-second cooldown, you'll likely want to go with a 60-second or 90-second cooldown and adjust for using it every 60, 90, or 120 seconds depending on the fight.
 
 

 

Windwalker Monk Starter Guide

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Windwalker Monk to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Windwalker Monk Major Cooldowns

Windwalker has access to a few abilities that count as longer cooldowns and not just rotational abilities. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the below section covers how they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.

 Zenith‎ 

 doesn't provide any direct damage increase without the addition of additional talents like the Apex Talents of Tigereye Brew . However, it does reduce the cost of all of your Chi spenders by 1 and increases the cooldown reduction provided by by an additional second. When you press the button it resets the cooldown of and provides you an additional 2 Chi to use right away.

Key takeaways are:
 
While is active, becomes free, so it is your primary filler in order to get and back from cooldown as quickly as possible.

This also means that you can very quickly feel like you have too much Chi if you're also using too often.
 

Due to getting your cooldowns back faster, it is even more important to have the Chi that you need to cast them right away.
If talented into then generates a Chi rather than consuming one. This causes it to function as both your primary filler and primary Chi-builder.

 has two stacks, so you do not need to use it as soon as it is available but can plan its use for the best possible time.

 Celestial Conduit

 is a powerful ability to use, but the most powerful aspect of it is that it adds the buff. However, because this buff can also come from using or , you need to stagger these uses for maximum benefit. This generally means using spaced out between casts of or . This attempts to insure maximum uptime and value.

The instance of that is triggered from using stacks with the version of that comes from , , or . However, the instance of that is generated from does not stack with the instance that comes from or .

This means that you can cast when you already have up, and you should because they stack very well. You want to try and avoid casting if you already have the buff that comes from or and visa versa.

Key takeaways are:
 
Try to cast during .

Try NOT to cast if you still have the buff from or .

Try NOT to cast or if you have the buff from .
 

 Invoke Xuen

With the changes in Midnight is mainly a button you press so that you can then channel afterwards. This means that you'll want to plan ahead slightly so that you are not wasting a GCD summoning Xuen when you want to be dealing damage.

There is a large window after casting where you're able to cast . Because balancing the above buff generally means a somewhat strict sequence of abilities, you will want to avoid deviating much from the above opener, even if it's the middle of a fight.

 Touch of Death

 seems like a straightforward ability to use but attempting to min/max it can lead to losing damage rather than gaining it. With the change to in Midnight, it no longer provides a damage increase after using it.

While this generally means that you'll want to use it as soon as its available and you have space to press it without delaying another ability, it also means that you CAN try to use it right before the target dies when your target has less health than your maximum health so that it deals 100% of your health rather than just the 35% of your maximum health that it deals if you use it on a target that is at 15% health or lower.

This is a very small window and can sometimes have a delay before being usable if you just swap to a target to try and hit it with . This delay can be the difference between making or missing the very small window. Missing the window generally means that you don't get off and thus lose damage that you would have done if you had cast it sooner.

 Touch of Karma

 is, first and foremost, a defensive ability. Its primary use is to absorb some damage in order to lessen the damage that you are dealt. However, the secondary function of is that some of the damage that the shield absorbs is redirected back to the target that you cast the spell on. This means that can be used offensively if you do not need its defensive value.

Most fights in most content have times where you will be taking damage and can cleanly use for both its defensive and offensive value. However, sometimes the damage you are taking isn't enough to necessitate a defensive cooldown like . In these situations it is, technically, optimal to find some damage that you can then absorb and redirect. This can be done through standing in some damage effect on the ground, or in extreme situations, casting on a target and taking a few smacks.

Needing to a target to get the benefit from should be used as a last resort and only ever be done with the express permission of your tanks and healers as you're often likely to get killed once the shield ends without direct intervention. Do this at your own risk. 

 Fortifying Brew

 increases your maximum health, so it also increases the damage that deals and that can absorb. Because of this, using before you use or is a damage increase. This can be used to further improve your defense in a time of need, but it also has the secondary effect of increasing the amount of damage that is redirected back to the target.

If you are not going to need the defensive value of on its own, like if large damage intake is more frequent and you need to stagger your defensive cooldowns, then you can stack them together for added benefit. Just be sure to use BEFORE using or as both snapshot on use.

A real good way to use this is to find a way to use then at a time when you'll also be able to use during the duration of . This gets you both benefits for one use. If you're already going to use it for DPS purposes, then you might as well be efficient about it.
